spec.title: Adventure, without the guesswork
spec.notes: These four cards represent our core value pillars. Local expertise means safety and authenticity—you're not following a guidebook, you're following someone who knows every switchback. Paced routes prevent the main cause of rescue: rushing altitude. Logistics removes the 'what if' anxiety that stops people from booking. Community connection transforms the trek from a personal conquest into a cultural exchange—and it keeps revenue in the region. Each card answers a specific fear: 'Will I be safe?' 'Can I actually do this?' 'What if something goes wrong?' 'Is this just another tourist experience?'

cards.heading: Local Mountain Expertise
cards.text: Our guides grew up on these trails. They read weather patterns in the sky, know every safe crossing, and speak the languages of villages along the route.

cards.heading: Carefully Paced Routes
cards.text: No forced marches. Itineraries build in acclimatization days, rest stops at comfortable altitudes, and flexibility for how each group feels.

cards.heading: Dependable Logistics
cards.text: Porters and pack animals organized before you arrive. Tents, food, permits, and emergency communications—all handled, so you focus on the climb.

cards.heading: Meaningful Community Connection
cards.text: Stay in locally owned teahouses, hire guides from surrounding villages, and support conservation projects that protect these landscapes.

slides.brief: Present the core experience through four visual cards: local mountain expertise, carefully paced routes, dependable logistics, and meaningful community connection. Keep the language concrete and benefit-led rather than generic.

spec.title: Every day earns the view
spec.notes: This timeline shows the arc of a typical trek—not a rigid itinerary, but the rhythm we create. Each step serves a purpose: rest prevents rushing, villages build connection, high camps earn the views. The icons guide you through the journey visually. In your pitch, emphasize that routes vary by season and group fitness—this is an example of how we structure time, not a promise of exact dates or every stop. Mention that we adjust day lengths and rest days based on how the group acclimates, so no one is forced beyond their pace.
spec.caption: Sample itinerary structure (routes and timing vary by season and group)

steps.label: Day 1–2
steps.heading: Arrival & Acclimatization
steps.text: Land in Kathmandu. Rest, explore, let your body adjust to altitude gradually.

steps.label: Day 3–4
steps.heading: Trail Begins
steps.text: Easy slopes, village tea stops, first mountain views. Your rhythm emerges.

steps.label: Day 5–7
steps.heading: High Camps & Discovery
steps.text: Climb higher. Sleep in teahouses. Meet locals. Weather shapes each day.

steps.label: Day 8–9
steps.heading: Summit Push & Reward
steps.text: Final ascent at dawn. Alpine meadows and peaks reveal themselves. The view earns every step.

steps.label: Day 10
steps.heading: Descent & Reflection
steps.text: Trail down. Energy returns. Stories crystallize. You're already planning the next one.

slides.brief: Show a sample trekking journey from arrival and acclimatization to trail days, village stays, and the final mountain viewpoint. Frame the itinerary as a rhythm of preparation, discovery, and reward; label it as an example route rather than a fixed promise.

spec.title: When the trail gets tough, we adapt
spec.notes: This slide directly addresses the fears that keep people from booking. Be specific: altitude sickness isn't just discomfort, it's the primary reason for evacuations, and our pacing protocol reduces incidents dramatically. Weather in the Himalayas can turn dangerous quickly—our guides don't rely on apps, they rely on decades of reading these mountains. Fatigue is cumulative and underestimated; we plan for it rather than pushing through. The logistics point is about dignity and safety: when you're exhausted and disoriented, you shouldn't have to negotiate a room or find water. Our ratio means someone is always watching out for you. Emphasize that 'flexible' isn't a buzzword—it's a safety protocol. We've rerouted entire groups mid-trek when conditions demanded it. No itinerary is worth risking a client's health.

left.heading: The challenges
bullets: Altitude sickness hits without warning—headaches, nausea, worse
Weather shifts from clear skies to whiteout in hours
Fatigue compounds daily; bodies don't recover like they do at sea level
Foreign trails, unfamiliar systems, language barriers at every turn

right.heading: Our response
bullets: Conservative pacing with built-in rest days and medical checks
Local guides read cloud formations and know shelter locations
Flexible itineraries—we add days, change routes, or pause as needed
One guide for every four trekkers; you're never figuring things out alone

'Can I actually do this?' 'What if something goes wrong?' 'Is this just another tourist experience?'

cards.heading: Local Mountain Expertise
cards.text: Our guides grew up on these trails. They read weather patterns in the sky, know every safe crossing, and speak the languages of villages along the route.

cards.heading: Carefully Paced Routes
cards.text: No forced marches. Itineraries build in acclimatization days, rest stops at comfortable altitudes, and flexibility for how each group feels.

cards.heading: Dependable Logistics
cards.text: Porters and pack animals organized before you arrive. Tents, food, permits, and emergency communications—all handled, so you focus on the climb.

cards.heading: Meaningful Community Connection
cards.text: Stay in locally owned teahouses, hire guides from surrounding villages, and support conservation projects that protect these landscapes.

spec.title: When the trail gets tough, we adapt
spec.notes: This slide directly addresses the fears that keep people from booking. Be specific: altitude sickness isn't just discomfort, it's the primary reason for evacuations, and our pacing protocol reduces incidents dramatically. Weather in the Himalayas can turn dangerous quickly—our guides don't rely on apps, they rely on decades of reading these mountains. Fatigue is cumulative and underestimated; we plan for it rather than pushing through. The logistics point is about dignity and safety: when you're exhausted and disoriented, you shouldn't have to negotiate a room or find water. Our ratio means someone is always watching out for you. Emphasize that 'flexible' isn't a buzzword—it's a safety protocol. We've rerouted entire groups mid-trek when conditions demanded it. No itinerary is worth risking a client's health.
